title: I–V characteristics
examples: What does the slope of the graph tell us about the component?
How is a diode different from a resistor on an I-V graph?
Can you explain what happens to the current when the voltage is zero?

explain.say: Today we will look at I-V characteristics graphs.
First we look at a simple resistor's graph.
The resistor graph is a straight line through the origin.
Next we examine the lamp's characteristic graph.
The diode graph shows a different, non-linear curve.
In daily life, we use these graphs to select components.

faq.q: What does the slope of the resistor graph mean?
faq.a: The slope of the resistor graph represents its resistance value. A steeper slope means higher resistance.
asks: How do I find the resistance from the graph?
Is the resistance equal to the slope?

faq.q: Why does the diode graph look so different from the resistor?
faq.a: The diode has a built-in junction that only allows current to flow easily in one direction. This causes the curve shape.
asks: Does the diode always behave like a resistor?
What makes the diode graph non-linear?

faq.q: What happens to the current if I reverse the voltage on a diode?
faq.a: If you reverse the voltage, the current through the diode will be very close to zero. This is called reverse bias.
asks: Can I pass current through a diode backwards?

faq.q: Are lamps always linear like resistors?
faq.a: No, lamps can behave non-linearly, especially when they get hot or change their internal resistance. They are not always perfect resistors.
asks: Does the lamp resistance change with temperature?
Is the lamp graph always a straight line?

faq.q: What is the relationship between voltage and current in general?
faq.a: Voltage is the electrical potential difference, and current is the flow of charge. They are related by the component's resistance.
asks: What does V stand for in this context?
How are voltage and current related?

facts: Resistors generally follow Ohm's Law, resulting in a linear I-V graph.
Diodes are semiconductor devices that allow current flow primarily in one direction.
The lamp's characteristic curve is often non-linear due to heating effects.
The resistance of a component can be calculated from the gradient of its I-V graph.

quiz.say: A component whose I-V graph is a straight line through the origin is most likely a:
quiz.why: A straight line indicates a constant ratio between voltage and current, which is Ohm's Law.

wrong.0: The diode graph is curved, not a straight line.
wrong.1: Lamps can show non-linear behavior depending on the current.
wrong.2: A battery is a source, not a component measured this way.

quiz.say: If the voltage across a diode is increased greatly in the forward direction, the current will:
quiz.why: Once past the knee voltage, the diode resistance drops, allowing current to increase quickly.

wrong.0: Current flow is measured as a positive value in this context.
wrong.2: This only happens in reverse bias or if the diode is broken.
wrong.3: The relationship is not generally decreasing in this region.

quiz.say: Which graph shows the current being nearly zero when the voltage is reversed?
quiz.why: The diode blocks current flow when the voltage polarity is reversed.

wrong.0: An ideal wire would show a straight line through the origin.
wrong.2: A resistor allows current to flow equally in both directions.
wrong.3: Lamps do not show a distinct zero-current region like a diode.
